newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Alfonsin leaves hospital after checks.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Alfonsin leaves hospital after checks.

text.p: Argentine former President Raul Alfonsin left on Saturday a Buenos Aires hospital where he was admitted a day earlier after a routine check-up detected heart problems.
"I am very, very well," he told reporters as he left the hospital.

The 69-year-old Radical Party leader, who was Argentina's first democratic president after military dictatorship ended in 1983, said: "Now I will have to follow a diet. I will have to eat He said instead of going home to Chascomus, a town about 120 miles (200 km) south of Buenos Aires, he would stay in Buenos Aires to finish a book he is writing on Argentine politics.
After losing an election to Peronist Carlos Menem in 1989, Alfonsin was forced by economic disarray to leave office six months before his term ended.
He is no longer head of the Radical Party, but is still one of its most powerful figures and has recently talked of making another bid for the Argentine presidency in 1999.
Famed for his oratory, Alfonsin drew a crowd of 30,000 to a Buenos Aires soccer stadium in November for a rally against the "neo-conservative" policies applied by Menem's government.
